name: Genoa: Le Strade Nuove and the system of the Palazzi dei Rolli
description: In the heart of Genoa, in northwest Italy, a row of grand Renaissance and Baroque palaces lines Via Garibaldi and Via Balbi, laid out when the seafaring Republic was at its richest. A 1576 Senate decree let the state lodge visiting dignitaries in these private mansions. Today you can walk through their stepped courtyards, staircases and gardens, and visit museums such as Palazzo Rosso and Palazzo Bianco.
